::: {.piege}
```{r}
c(1, 2, )
paste("a", "b", )
which(1, TRUE, TRUE, )
```
:::

## Why

To R, a trailing comma is not a syntax error: it opens one more argument, left empty. Each function then reacts in its own way to that missing argument.

`c()` reports that "argument 3 is empty", `paste()` that an argument is missing, with no default. `which()`, which has no `...`, receives one argument too many and answers `unused argument (alist())`. None of these messages mentions a comma.

## The remedy

Remove the trailing comma, especially after deleting or commenting out the last line of a call written over several lines.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
c(1, 2)
paste("a", "b")
```
:::
